text:
Jackson LaCombe has become Anaheim's everything defenseman. He's playing 27 and a half minutes a night, up from just over 24 last season, and almost 29 over his last ten games, including 33 against Edmonton. He's on the ice for 82% of the Ducks' power-play time, and the assists have followed: 21 of his 22 points, 15 of them in the last ten.

Some of that is a role that stays and some is luck that won't. Anaheim has scored 8.9 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and his scoring rate is well above the range our numbers think he can hold. The bigger warning sign is five on five: the Ducks get only 37.5% of the expected goals with him out there, nearly 12 points worse than when he sits. Heavy minutes explain some of that, not all.

Last season told a better story. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 94th percentile among defensemen for driving expected goals, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the best passers at his position. Watch whether the even-strength numbers recover. That will decide whether this is a breakout or an overload.
headline: Twenty-seven minutes a night and climbing
